Kurunegala.fact: The largest among them is Ethagala or the "Elephant Rock" (though the translation is actually tusker), reaches 325 metres (1,066 ft). The shape of Ethagala resembles an elephant.

Kurunegala.subject: Ancient India
Kurunegala.question: Its ascendancy as an ancient capital of _____ began with a series of events that took place during the late 12th century at Yapahuwa
Kurunegala.fact: Its ascendancy as an ancient capital of Sri Lanka began with a series of events that took place during the late 12th century at Yapahuwa. Over the next half a century Kurunegala was the capital and the governing centre for three other kings of Sri Lanka.

Kurunegala.subject: Ancient India
Kurunegala.question: The sacred tooth relic which was in the Yapahuwa Kingdom was taken by an Aryacakravarti from the Jaffna Kingdom to the Pandyan country during the rule of Buwaneka Bahu I from _____ to 1284
Kurunegala.fact: The sacred tooth relic which was in the Yapahuwa Kingdom was taken by an Aryacakravarti from the Jaffna Kingdom to the Pandyan country during the rule of Buwaneka Bahu I from 1272 to 1284.

Kurunegala.subject: Ancient India
Kurunegala.question: The relic was brought back by King Parakrama Bahu III who ruled from Kurunegala between _____ and 1293
Kurunegala.fact: The relic was brought back by King Parakrama Bahu III who ruled from Kurunegala between 1287 and 1293.

Kurunegala.subject: Ancient India
Kurunegala.question: After the death of King Parakrama Bahu III, King Buwanekabahu II (_____–1302), followed by Parakramabahu IV (1302–1326), ruled from Kurunegala
Kurunegala.fact: The relic was brought back by King Parakrama Bahu III who ruled from Kurunegala between 1287 and 1293. After the death of King Parakrama Bahu III, King Buwanekabahu II (1293–1302), followed by Parakramabahu IV (1302–1326), ruled from Kurunegala.

Kurunegala.subject: Ancient India
Kurunegala.question: The ruler in Kurunegala from _____ to 1335 was Buwanekabahu III, also known as Wanni Buwanekabahu
Kurunegala.fact: After the death of King Parakrama Bahu III, King Buwanekabahu II (1293–1302), followed by Parakramabahu IV (1302–1326), ruled from Kurunegala. The ruler in Kurunegala from 1326 to 1335 was Buwanekabahu III, also called Wanni Buwanekabahu.

Kurunegala.subject: Ancient India
Kurunegala.question: After the reign of Buwaneka Bahu III, the newly throned king Vijayabahu V ruled from Dambadeniya and Yapahuwa from _____ to 1341 before once again the kingdom of Sri Lanka shifted to Gampola
Kurunegala.fact: The ruler in Kurunegala from 1326 to 1335 was Buwanekabahu III, also called Wanni Buwanekabahu. After the reign of Buwaneka Bahu III, the newly throned king Vijayabahu V ruled from Dambadeniya and Yapahuwa from 1335 to 1341 before once again the kingdom of Sri Lanka shifted to Gampola.

Kurunegala.fact: During the month of April the temperature can rise up to about 35 °C (95 °F).

Kurunegala.subject: Ancient India
Kurunegala.question: While the city does experience noticeably drier weather during _____ and February, it does not qualify as a true dry season as average precipitation in both months are above 60 millimetres (2 in)
Kurunegala.fact: The only major change in the Kurunegala weather occurs during the monsoons from May to August and October to January when heavy rains can be expected. While the city does experience noticeably drier weather during January and February, it does not qualify as a true dry season as average precipitation in both months are above 60 millimetres (2 in).

Kurunegala.fact: Residents from ethnic minorities live in all parts of the city, however, sizeable communities of Moors and Tamils live in the areas of Teliyagonna and Wilgoda.
